rows.heading: # VisualCore Suite — Claude Code Desktop repository instructions
rows.note: D-10 (C-09): replaced by the bootstrap CLAUDE.md and Auto-Creator.md; README.md is no longer the specification. Kept as CLAUDE.md rule 8: Claude Desktop Code only, never the CLI, Agent SDK or model-calling Python.

rows.heading: ## 0. Starting a session and the standing owner rules — read first
rows.note: Lives on as CLAUDE.md section 2 (live state) and rules 7, 11, 13, 14. Rule 4 'push to origin main' is suspended by D-13 (C-08). Lessons (tick_task prefix, 2-chunk regression, SC-F702 rerun, per-frame state) are in AC-19.

rows.heading: ## 1. Mission and order of operations
rows.note: D-01, D-02 (C-01): 25 separately built apps become experiences of one app, 100 at launch. D-07, D-08 (C-04): the 25-app lock and 75 device rows become ImplementationLock-100 and 300 rows. Kept: no device before the lock.

rows.heading: ## 2. Operating Claude Desktop
rows.note: Binding: Auto mode without bypass, one writing session, at most 10 agents, one writer per file, one Xcode lane, no self-spawning schedules, foreground builds of 10 minutes or less, never stop. Optional scheduled task.

rows.heading: ## 3. Governing documents and conflicts
rows.note: D-10 (C-09): Auto-Creator.md, ADR-0009 and the bootstrap CLAUDE.md replace the README chapters and this contract in the precedence order. Carried: toolchain behaviour first; never drop a hard requirement (D-14).

rows.heading: ## 4. Hard architecture boundaries
rows.note: Binding (D-09): GLES via ANGLE-Metal only, no second renderer or public EGL bridge; projectm-ios pinned read-only; Vendor/angle untouched; ProjectM out of the API; reuse rules in AC-13. Per-app targets end with D-01.

rows.heading: ## 5. Public API, privacy, licensing and safety rules
rows.note: Binding: public Apple APIs only (no dlopen/dlsym, ReplayKit workarounds); 10-minute non-silent device export before an audio-source claim; owner-provisioned signing; licences; built-app privacy audit. Networking: D-15.

rows.heading: ## 6. Exact three-device acceptance matrix
rows.note: D-08 keeps D1 iPhone15,4, D2 iPad17,3 and D3 iPad15,7 (never updated from iPadOS 26.5) in that order; 25 apps per device (75 rows) become 100 experiences per device (300 rows, C-04). The roster is final.

rows.heading: ## 7. Spec Kit in the Desktop Code session
rows.note: Binding: installed speckit-* skills run in the Desktop session with the verbatim prompt plus 'Canonical override:' notes, one feature per gate, converge loop until nothing is appended. D-11 extends the numbering.

rows.heading: ## 8. Implementation campaign: development checks allowed, device tests not allowed
rows.note: D-07, D-12 (C-04): the order F00-F09, 175 app gates, implementation lock becomes the 100-experience simulator gate; push to origin main is suspended by D-13 (C-08). Kept: host and simulator checks only before the lock.

rows.heading: ## 9. Batched physical-device campaign: automation details
rows.note: Planned as UA-F13: run_device_campaign.py refuses before the lock; devicectl discovery by productType; 200 samples; CADisplayLink meter; container privacy check. 75 jobs become 300 (D-08). AutomationRunner exists (F09).

rows.heading: ## 10. Evidence, checkpoints, and finish conditions
rows.note: run-check, seal, record and the log and failure rules stay for both ledgers (D-12). desktop_runbook.py and .autonomy exist and sealed F00-F09 and A01-P00..A04-P03. The report over 25 apps and 75 rows: superseded (C-04).

rows.heading: ## 11. App portfolio (all required; detailed instructions in the preserved README appendices)
rows.note: All 25 stay required as the free experiences A01-A25 (D-02), no longer separate apps (D-01, C-01). A01-A03 are sealed, A04 through P03; A04-P04..A25-P06 remain. Kept: read the app's own manual (embedded/apps) first.

rows.heading: ## 12. Reference evidence and historical context — do not launder into new test results
rows.note: ProjectM-iOS history: Stage 1 go, ANGLE Gate 3, 1.0 uploaded, D1 audio test at 7.4% CPU, captures shorter than the 10-minute gate. Never VisualCore evidence; that guard is CLAUDE.md rule 9 and D-08.

rows.heading: ## 13. Copyable continuation instruction for Desktop Code
rows.note: Replaced by the AC-28 continuation prompt (D-10, C-09). The old text names README.md, 175 app phases, the 25-app lock and 75 device rows (C-01, C-04). Carried: never the CLI, no device test before the lock, checkpoints.

rows.heading: ## 14. Original ProjectM-iOS playbook — complete verbatim source (2026-11-10)
rows.note: Provenance wrapper. SHA-256 8f691031... is the whole 381-line ProjectM-iOS CLAUDE.md (embedded/sources); section 14 holds its lines 170-381, also extracted to docs/archive/planning/playbook. Its approvals do not apply.

rows.heading: ## Playbook: a new iOS app with Claude and Spec Kit, little human interaction (2026-11-10)
rows.note: Container of the lessons the owner wants integrated: Spec Kit and simulator AC-19; setup, CI, release, owner actions AC-24; StoreKit AC-14; devices AC-23; performance AC-12. Their home is now Auto-Creator.md (D-10).

rows.heading: ### Owner rules and standing approvals (ask once, record here)
rows.note: Carry: commit per task or skill with 'Feature NNN Txxx: change' subjects, no trailers, owner's git email, LF, [skip ci] only on docs-only pushes, dated owner rulings, owner-only list. Push approval: history (D-13).

rows.heading: ### Spec Kit flow (one feature, start to finish)
rows.note: Carry: guidance with a ready prompt per command first; eight skills in order; per-feature id ranges checked by validate_docs.py (D-11 here); {device} and {owner} tags closed honestly; an agent report is not evidence.

rows.heading: ### Project setup that keeps humans out
rows.note: Carry: XcodeGen with gitignored .xcodeproj, logic in Packages/ (AC-16), Signing.xcconfig '#include?' pattern, CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO off-device, name before the permanent bundle id, version keys in prebuilt frameworks.

rows.heading: ### CI (GitHub Actions, `.github/workflows/ios-ci.yml`)
rows.note: Carry: concurrency with cancel-in-progress and timeout-minutes on every job, fast docs and compliance gate, cached xcframework builds, XcodeGen pinned by SHA-256, simulator by runtime, gh run watch <id> --exit-status.

rows.heading: ### Testing on the Mac (simulators)
rows.note: Carry: xcodebuild output to a log file, -test-timeouts-enabled YES -default-test-execution-time-allowance 180, hang triage, simctl privacy reset and erase, XCUITest pitfalls. SKTestSession isolation rules go to AC-14.

rows.heading: ### Automated device testing (devicectl, no Xcode UI)
rows.note: Carry: runner under DEBUG || *_AUTOMATION started by *_AUTORUN, nm -U check, devicectl list, install, launch and copy commands, hardwareProperties.udid for xcodebuild, 200 samples, CADisplayLink meter, thinning report.

rows.heading: ### App Store Connect and release
rows.note: Carry into UA-F14: early name check (OD-01), icon, ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption, privacy manifest of the built app, privacy policy URL, EULA, review notes, exact-size screenshots, Paid Apps agreement. No agent-run ASC.

rows.heading: ### Performance lessons from feature 002
rows.note: Carry: readiness means what the user needs (local entitlement, not the price); parallel start-up work (async let); build-time data in display order; load and first frame measured separately. The D1 timings are history.
